briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with multiple reports indicating no commercial vessel traffic since Tuesday, raising global energy security concerns. Diplomatic efforts are ongoing, with Iran evaluating a US proposal, while military posturing continues in the Persian Gulf and along the Israel-Lebanon border, where a Hezbollah drone attack seriously injured an Israeli reservist.

IRAN
US military confirmed disabling two Iranian tankers, Sea Star III and Sevda, on May 8, and the Hasna on May 6, preventing their entry into Iranian ports. The US also announced sanctions against 10 individuals and companies, including those from China and Hong Kong, for aiding Iran's Shahed drone and ballistic missile programs. Iran's Foreign Ministry denounced US actions in the Persian Gulf as ceasefire violations and warned against continued military provocations, asserting the US no longer has the right to use the Strait of Hormuz for attacks. Iran's UN ambassador stated the country retains the right to self-defense against US naval maneuvers. Mohammad Mokhber, an assistant to the Supreme Leader, reportedly claimed the Strait of Hormuz holds power equivalent to an atomic bomb. Reports from CNN and Kian Meli 1 indicate Iran sent radio messages warning vessels to stay 10 miles from US warships, stating the need "to teach Yankees a lesson" with "missiles and drones."

Internally, Iranian media and US intelligence reports continue to discuss the health of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, noting severe burns to one side of his body, and that he communicates only via face-to-face meetings or messengers. Mojtaba Khamenei, his son, is reported to be playing a critical role in shaping war strategy, and suffered injuries to his knee, back, and behind his ear, with his wife allegedly killed, during a bombing of Ali Khamenei's residence. Iran's internet shutdown entered its 11th week, causing significant economic damage, estimated at 55 trillion tomans in lost revenue for the digital economy. Pakistan increased fuel prices, with gasoline now 414 rupees per liter. Iran confirmed its participation in the 2026 World Cup, setting conditions including visa issuance, respect for the national flag and anthem, and enhanced security.

ISRAEL
Three IDF reservists were wounded, one seriously, and two moderately, by an explosive drone launched by Hezbollah near the Lebanon border today. Another Hezbollah explosive drone struck an unmanned IDF engineering vehicle, causing damage. In separate incidents, two additional Hezbollah explosive drones were located in Israeli territory without causing damage or injuries. Air defenses intercepted several rockets launched by Hezbollah at troops in southern Lebanon. An earlier hostile aircraft intrusion alert in Arab al-Aramshe was later declared a false alarm, with an interceptor missile launched at a "false target." IDF spokesperson stated that in the last 24 hours, Israel struck over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon and an underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley. Israeli media (N12) reported that Israel will release two participants of the Gaza flotilla, a Spanish and a Brazilian citizen, after questioning. Wizz Air cancelled flights to Israel until May 26.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF forces, in cooperation with the Shin Bet, destroyed a weapon manufacturing and storage site belonging to Palestinian Islamic Jihad in the northern Gaza Strip yesterday. This site was also used by Hamas for producing explosives. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers reportedly burned homes and cars and attacked a Palestinian child. Israeli forces compelled a Palestinian family in the northern West Bank to exhume their son’s grave and move the body to another location. UN reports indicate that Israel has displaced 40,000 Palestinians in the West Bank since the start of 2025. Al-Shati refugee camp in Gaza City has suffered widespread destruction from Israeli attacks, forcing residents to sleep on the streets.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched explosive drones and rockets into northern Israel and at Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, resulting in three injured Israeli reservists, one seriously, and damage to an unmanned engineering vehicle. Hezbollah released videos showing attacks on Israeli Merkava tanks in Al-Biyada and Alma al-Shaab with attack drones, claiming two tanks were hit and burned. Israeli occupation aircraft reportedly bombarded several towns in southern Lebanon, with Press TV reporting at least 11 civilians killed in Al-Saksakieh and a total of 20 more civilians martyred across southern Lebanon, including a civil defense rescuer, despite a ceasefire agreement. The IDF announced striking over 85 Hezbollah infrastructures in southern Lebanon and an underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley over the last 24 hours, targeting weapon depots, rocket launchers, and buildings used by Hezbollah, as well as operatives planning attacks.

SYRIA & IRAQ
An Iraqi governmental committee, including the outgoing and incoming Prime Ministers (Al-Sudani and Al-Zaidi) and Hadi Al-Amri, is reportedly close to completing a plan to disarm pro-Iranian militias, to be presented to the Trump administration. Iraqi border guards intercepted an air balloon carrying over 34 kg of Captagon pills (198,000 pills) from Syria. An MQ-9 drone and AH-64 Apache helicopters were spotted over Baghdad. Iranian Kurdish opposition headquarters in Erbil, northern Iraq, were reportedly hit by drone attacks. The Russian embassy in Baghdad posted a photo with the hashtag #Russia_Iraq_cannot_be_separated, celebrating Victory Day.

GULF STATES
Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced the arrest of 41 individuals allegedly linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry expressed full support for Bahrain's actions against Iranian-linked activities. Kuwait reduced marine vessel traffic due to fear of Iranian attacks. Qatar's affiliated LNG carrier loaded at Ras Laffan is reportedly navigating the Iran-approved northern route near Qeshm and Larak Islands, marking Qatar's first known LNG export via the Strait of Hormuz since the war began. The UAE held a "Made in Emirates" event in Abu Dhabi, attracting $46 billion in investments across various sectors, surpassing Iran's projected oil revenue for 2025. Gulf states reportedly spent an additional $17 billion on 4,200 Patriot missiles, indicating preparation for potential conflict.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Closure:** No commercial vessels run by registered shipping companies have crossed the Strait of Hormuz since Tuesday, May 6, according to the Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg.
2.  **US Strikes on Iranian Tankers:** US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed disabling two Iranian tankers (Sea Star III, Sevda) on May 8 and another (Hasna) on May 6, citing enforcement of a naval blockade.
3.  **Hezbollah Drone Attack in Israel:** An explosive drone launched by Hezbollah seriously wounded one Israeli reservist and moderately injured two others near the Lebanon border on May 9.
4.  **IDF Strikes in Lebanon:** The IDF reported striking over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon and an underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley in the last 24 hours.
5.  **Bahraini Arrests:** Bahrain announced the arrest of 41 individuals allegedly linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
6.  **Mojtaba Khamenei's Injuries:** Reports indicate Mojtaba Khamenei sustained injuries (knee, back, ear) during a bombing of the Supreme Leader's residence, where his wife was allegedly killed.
7.  **Iran Evaluating US Proposal:** Iran's Foreign Ministry stated it has received and is reviewing the US's proposal to end the conflict, with the US expecting a response by today.
8.  **UK Warship Deployment:** The UK announced it will redeploy HMS Dragon, a Type 45 destroyer, to the Middle East for a potential role in safeguarding shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
9.  **Strait of Hormuz Threats:** Iran's IRGC issued radio warnings to vessels to maintain a 10-mile distance from US warships due to potential missile and drone attacks.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain extremely high, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, which is effectively closed to commercial shipping. The US's continued enforcement of a naval blockade and Iran's warnings to international shipping create a volatile environment ripe for direct military confrontation. The Israeli-Hezbollah front is actively escalating, with Hezbollah's use of explosive drones causing casualties and Israel responding with extensive airstrikes into Lebanon. Both sides' military postures suggest a readiness for deeper engagement. Iran's economic vulnerabilities due to the blockade and internet cutoffs could lead to internal instability or more aggressive external actions. US red lines appear to be direct threats to American personnel, while Iran views US naval presence and strikes as provocative violations of the ceasefire. The potential UN Security Council resolution on the Strait of Hormuz could further formalize international pressure on Iran, possibly leading to more retaliatory measures.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture:** President Trump expressed a strong desire for the war with Iran to end and stated the US is awaiting Iran's response to its proposal, warning that failure to reach an agreement would lead to "Freedom Project Plus." The US imposed new sanctions on 10 individuals and companies involved in Iran's drone and missile programs, including entities in China and Hong Kong. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated that US military actions against Iran would remain "defensive" in response to attacks on American forces and condemned Iran's claims over the Strait of Hormuz.
**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia officially backed Bahrain's actions against Iran-linked individuals. Gulf states, including the UAE, continue to bolster their defenses, with significant investments in missile defense systems.
**EU Members:** Germany and France, as part of a joint initiative, are coordinating with the UK to ensure the security of the Strait of Hormuz, with the UK deploying HMS Dragon to the region. European leaders are increasingly concerned about the economic impact of the conflict and US unpredictability.
**Russia:** Russia agreed to a three-day ceasefire in Ukraine (May 9-11) as proposed by Trump, to include an exchange of 1,000 prisoners from each side. Russia's UN ambassador stated Moscow would object to a US-Bahraini draft resolution on Iran in the Security Council, arguing it would not achieve maritime security. Russian officials indicated increased contact with Washington regarding Ukrainian threats.
**China:** Chinese firms and individuals faced US sanctions for allegedly assisting Iran's defense sector, specifically its drone program. China's Defense Ministry urged Japan to confront its history and curb military expansionism.
**Turkey:** Turkey's President Erdoğan met with Iraqi Kurdistan Prime Minister Masrour Barzani to discuss bilateral relations and regional developments. Turkey also reportedly unveiled a new intercontinental missile, "Yildirimann," with claims of a 6000 km range and a 3000 kg warhead, though military experts expressed skepticism.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several unverified claims and contradictions were observed.
*   **Khamenei's Health:** While N12 and CNN report Khamenei's injuries and isolation, the specific details regarding Mojtaba Khamenei's injuries and his wife's death during a bombing of the residence (Vahid Online) are highly specific and attributed to a "responsible for meetings" official, but still from a single source's reporting of internal Iranian claims. The extent and exact nature of injuries and events remain difficult to independently confirm.
*   **Minab School Attack:** The US is investigating the attack on a school in Minab. Vahid Online quotes a Minab governor reporting one sailor killed and four missing from a cargo dhow, and 10 injured, without mentioning schoolchildren. Press TV, however, reports 120 students and 26 female teachers killed in a "US-Israeli massacre" at a school in Minab, claiming it could have been a planned strike. These accounts are directly contradictory regarding the targets and casualties of the Minab incident, highlighting a significant reporting gap and potential propaganda.
*   **Oil Spill vs. Discharge:** Press TV and Vahid Online report a significant oil spill near Khark Island. Shargh Daily quotes the head of the Energy Committee denying an official report of a spill, while NAYA quotes an Iranian MP attributing satellite images of oil near Khark Island to an "European tanker" discharging contaminated water. This is a direct contradiction regarding the source and nature of the oil in the Persian Gulf.
*   **Strait of Hormuz Status:** While Bloomberg and WSJ (via Faytuks, Kian Meli) report no commercial vessel traffic since Tuesday, Shargh Daily states no major commercial ship has passed for "two consecutive days," implying a slightly shorter duration than other reports.
*   **Iranian Rallies:** Press TV publishes viewpoints on "epic rallies" across Iran, describing them as "powerful revolutionary momentum" ignored by Western pundits, possibly indicating a propaganda effort to counter narratives of internal dissent.
